question: Which of the following has straight-chain hydrocarbons?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Butane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Butane** is a straight-chain hydrocarbon belonging to the alkane family. Its chemical formula is **C4H10**, and it consists of four carbon atoms arranged in a continuous chain.
 
• **3-Methylpentane**, **2-Methylpropane**, and **Isobutane** are branched-chain hydrocarbons. They contain substituent groups attached to the main chain, making them different from straight-chain hydrocarbons. *Hence, these options are incorrect.*
 
• In straight-chain hydrocarbons, all the carbon atoms are connected in a linear sequence without any branching. This structure is characteristic of **Butane**.
 
• **Isomerism**: While butane has isomers such as **Isobutane**, the straight-chain structure specifically refers to the unbranched form of butane.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Butane.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hydrocarbons:**

 
 
• Hydrocarbons are organic compounds composed entirely of carbon and hydrogen atoms. They are classified as alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes based on the type of bonding between carbon atoms.
 
• **Alkanes** are saturated hydrocarbons with single bonds between carbon atoms, while alkenes and alkynes have double and triple bonds, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Straight-chain hydrocarbons:**
 
 
• Straight-chain hydrocarbons have no branching in their structure. Examples include methane, ethane, propane, and butane.
 
• They are usually named using the **IUPAC nomenclature system**, where the prefix indicates the number of carbon atoms in the chain.
 
 
 
• **Branched-chain hydrocarbons:**
 
 
• In branched-chain hydrocarbons, substituent groups (such as methyl or ethyl groups) are attached to the main chain.
 
• Examples include **3-Methylpentane**, **2-Methylpropane**, and **Isobutane**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Butane:**
 
 
• **Butane** is commonly used as a fuel in lighters and portable stoves.
 
• It is also used in the production of **liquefied petroleum gas (LPG)** and as a raw material in the petrochemical industry.
 
 
 
• **Isomerism in Butane:**
 
 
• Butane has two isomers: **n-Butane** (straight-chain) and **Isobutane** (branched-chain).
 
• Both isomers exhibit different physical properties, such as boiling points and melting points, due to differences in molecular structure.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Alkane Naming Conventions:** Alkanes are named based on the number of carbon atoms in the longest continuous chain. Prefixes like "meth-", "eth-", "prop-", and "but-" indicate one, two, three, and four carbon atoms, respectively.
 
• **Physical Properties:** Straight-chain hydrocarbons generally have higher boiling points than their branched-chain counterparts due to stronger intermolecular forces.
 
• **Environmental Impact:** Combustion of hydrocarbons such as butane releases **carbon dioxide (CO2)**, a greenhouse gas contributing to global warming.
 
• **Industrial Usage:** Hydrocarbons like butane are widely used in the manufacturing of plastics, synthetic rubber, and other chemical products.
